request: 2 apples and a pear cost 80p, an apple and a pear cost 55p: what does each cost?

beats.intent: A bar of two apple blocks and a pear block, 80p altogether
beats.narration: Two apples and a pear cost eighty pence.
beats.code:
stage.title("Apples and pears")
k = 0.06
x0 = -6
row1 = VGroup(Rectangle(width=25 * k, height=0.7, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5), Rectangle(width=25 * k, height=0.7, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5), Rectangle(width=30 * k, height=0.7, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([x0 + 40 * k, 1.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(row1))
stage.add(row1)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text(t, font_size=24).move_to(b)) for b, t in zip(row1, ("apple", "apple", "pear"))])
stage.label(row1, "80p", direction=RIGHT)

beats.intent: A second bar, apple and pear, 55p, lined up under the right-hand end of the first
beats.narration: One apple and a pear cost fifty five pence. Line it up under the first bar.
beats.code:
row2 = VGroup(Rectangle(width=25 * k, height=0.7, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5), Rectangle(width=30 * k, height=0.7, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
row2.move_to([row1.get_right()[0] - row2.width / 2, 0.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(row2))
stage.add(row2)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text(t, font_size=24).move_to(b)) for b, t in zip(row2, ("apple", "pear"))])
stage.label(row2, "55p", direction=RIGHT)

beats.intent: The extra apple in the first bar highlighted: 80 − 55 = 25p
beats.narration: The only difference between the bars is one apple. So one apple costs eighty minus fifty five: twenty five pence. Then the pear is fifty five minus twenty five, thirty.
beats.code:
extra = SurroundingRectangle(row1[0], color=YELLOW, buff=0.06)
stage.play(Create(extra))
stage.add(extra)
stage.label(extra, "80 − 55 = 25p", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The bars beside 2a + p = 80, a + p = 55, so a = 25 and p = 30
beats.narration: Subtracting one equation from the other removes the pear: a is twenty five and p is thirty.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"2a + p = 80", r"a + p = 55", r"a = 25, \ p = 30")

request: why does a line from the centre at right angles to a chord cut it in half?

beats.intent: A circle of radius 5 with a chord AB across its lower part
beats.narration: Draw a circle of radius five and a chord A B across it.
beats.code:
stage.title("The perpendicular to a chord")
u = 0.44
c = np.array([-3, 0.3, 0])
circle = Circle(radius=5 * u, color=WHITE).move_to(c)
A = c + np.array([-4 * u, -3 * u, 0])
B = c + np.array([4 * u, -3 * u, 0])
chord = Line(A, B, color=BLUE, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(Create(circle), Create(chord))
stage.add(circle, chord)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("A", font_size=26).next_to(A, DL, buff=0.1)), FadeIn(Text("B", font_size=26).next_to(B, DR, buff=0.1)), FadeIn(Dot(c)), FadeIn(Text("O", font_size=26).next_to(c, UP, buff=0.1)))

beats.intent: A line from the centre O meeting the chord at M at a right angle
beats.narration: From the centre O, drop a line that meets the chord at right angles, at M.
beats.code:
M = c + np.array([0, -3 * u, 0])
om = Line(c, M, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(om))
stage.add(om)
ra = RightAngle(Line(M, B), Line(M, c), length=0.22, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(ra), FadeIn(Text("M", font_size=26).next_to(M, DOWN, buff=0.12)))
stage.add(ra)
stage.label(om, "3", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Radii OA and OB, both 5, forming two right triangles shaded in two colours
beats.narration: Join O to A and to B. Both are radii, five each, so the two right angled triangles share O M and have equal hypotenuses.
beats.code:
t1 = Polygon(c, A, M, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3)
t2 = Polygon(c, B, M, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.3)
stage.play(FadeIn(t1), FadeIn(t2))
stage.add(t1, t2)
stage.label(Line(c, A), "5", direction=LEFT, color=GREEN)
stage.label(Line(c, B), "5", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: The picture beside AM² = 5² − 3² = 16, so AM = MB = 4
beats.narration: By Pythagoras, A M squared is five squared minus three squared, sixteen, and so is M B squared. Both are four: the chord is cut exactly in half.

beats.intent: A rectangle 3 tall and x + 4 wide
beats.narration: Three times x plus four is the area of a rectangle three tall and x plus four wide.
beats.code:
stage.title("Expanding 3(x + 4)")
h = 1.8
wx, w4 = 2.6, 2.4
tl = np.array([-5.5, 0.9, 0])
rect = Rectangle(width=wx + w4, height=h, color=WHITE).move_to(tl + np.array([(wx + w4) / 2, -h / 2, 0]))
stage.play(Create(rect))
stage.add(rect)
stage.label(Line(tl, tl + h * DOWN), "3", direction=LEFT)
stage.label(Line(tl, tl + (wx + w4) * RIGHT), "x + 4", direction=UP)

beats.intent: The rectangle split into an x part and a 4 part
beats.narration: Split the width into its two parts, x and four.
beats.code:
cut = DashedLine(tl + wx * RIGHT, tl + wx * RIGHT + h * DOWN, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(cut))
stage.add(cut)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("x", font_size=28, color=BLUE).move_to(tl + np.array([wx / 2, -h - 0.35, 0]))), FadeIn(Text("4", font_size=28, color=ORANGE).move_to(tl + np.array([wx + w4 / 2, -h - 0.35, 0]))))

beats.intent: The two parts filled with their areas, 3x and 12
beats.narration: The left part is three by x, area three x. The right part is three by four, area twelve.
beats.code:
left = Rectangle(width=wx, height=h, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0).move_to(tl + np.array([wx / 2, -h / 2, 0]))
right = Rectangle(width=w4, height=h, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0).move_to(tl + np.array([wx + w4 / 2, -h / 2, 0]))
stage.play(FadeIn(left), FadeIn(right))
stage.add(left, right)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("3x", font_size=34).move_to(left)), FadeIn(Text("12", font_size=34).move_to(right)))

beats.intent: The rectangle beside 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12, and a check with x = 2: 18 = 18
beats.narration: So three times x plus four is three x plus twelve: multiply each part inside the bracket. Check with x equals two: three times six is eighteen, and six plus twelve is eighteen.

beats.intent: A single unit cube and a 2 by 2 by 2 cube: 1 and 8
beats.narration: A cube number is how many little cubes build a bigger cube. One on its own, then two by two by two: eight.
beats.code:
stage.title("Cube numbers")
e = 0.34
q = np.array([0.45 * e, 0.45 * e, 0])
cube = lambda n, o: VGroup(
    *[Square(e, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=1).move_to(o + np.array([(i + 0.5) * e, (j + 0.5) * e, 0])) for i in range(n) for j in range(n)],
    *[Polygon(o + np.array([i * e, n * e, 0]) + d * q, o + np.array([(i + 1) * e, n * e, 0]) + d * q, o + np.array([(i + 1) * e, n * e, 0]) + (d + 1) * q, o + np.array([i * e, n * e, 0]) + (d + 1) * q, color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=0.35, stroke_width=1) for i in range(n) for d in range(n)],
    *[Polygon(o + np.array([n * e, j * e, 0]) + d * q, o + np.array([n * e, j * e, 0]) + (d + 1) * q, o + np.array([n * e, (j + 1) * e, 0]) + (d + 1) * q, o + np.array([n * e, (j + 1) * e, 0]) + d * q, color=BLUE_D, fill_opacity=0.35, stroke_width=1) for j in range(n) for d in range(n)])
base = -1.6
c1 = cube(1, np.array([-6.3, base, 0]))
c2 = cube(2, np.array([-5.4, base, 0]))
stage.play(FadeIn(c1), FadeIn(c2))
stage.add(c1, c2)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("1", font_size=28).move_to([-6.1, base - 0.4, 0])), FadeIn(Text("8", font_size=28).move_to([-5.05, base - 0.4, 0])))

beats.narration: Three by three by three: twenty seven.
beats.code:
c3 = cube(3, np.array([-4.1, base, 0]))
stage.play(FadeIn(c3, lag_ratio=0.02))
stage.add(c3)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("27", font_size=28).move_to([-3.55, base - 0.4, 0])))

beats.narration: Four by four by four: sixty four. The numbers grow fast, because every edge grows at once.
beats.code:
c4 = cube(4, np.array([-2.3, base, 0]))
stage.play(FadeIn(c4, lag_ratio=0.02))
stage.add(c4)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("64", font_size=28).move_to([-1.6, base - 0.4, 0])))

beats.narration: These are n cubed: one, eight, twenty seven, sixty four. Next is five cubed, a hundred and twenty five.
